agree.reason: The plain apology, which names the six thin weeks and the single email, and the new credit and weekly-email promises speak directly to this household's grievance that the farm went quiet, so many would reconsider, though some may still want something for last year's losses.

honest.reason: Every figure and promise matches what Sam supplied, and the email openly admits that crop loss could happen again and that the nets don't cover the greens.

works_the_facts.reason: It lists the facts but never works them out for this reader: boxes cut by half clear the one-third threshold, so under the new policy last July's six weeks would have earned credit (roughly $147 of a $540 share), and it doesn't say so.

right_comparison.reason: It implicitly sets last year's silence and lack of credit against this year's policy, but it never states that comparison concretely, for example what the same storm would mean under the new rules.

qualification.reason: The hedge is specific and checkable: crop loss may still happen, the greens are unprotected, a weather cut of more than a third triggers credit, and the reader will hear from Sam that same week.

objections.reason: It meets the core objection that the farm went quiet and paid nothing with the weekly email and the credit threshold, and it raises no objection the facts already answer, though it leaves open whether anything is owed for last year.

fit.reason: It's a short email of about 195 words with a clear subject line and closing details (price, deadline, shares left, sign-up link), so it fits under the 200-word limit.
